ALG034 to Q16 bounded paid source adapter
13 October 2026
CANDIDATE PENDING INDEPENDENT REVIEW

Result

This packet supplies the production boundary excluded by the accepted paid
source bridge: an exact in-memory parser, complete dense numerator validation,
paid normalization and nearest-even requantization, immutable nested Q16 source
construction, producer-contract consistency checks, exact target-budget status,
and rejection receipts retaining every reached integer width. It is a bounded
implementation candidate, not a new mathematical acceptance.

The deployed v1 domain deliberately limits M to 4096 and numerator magnitude
width to 65536 bits. These are public supported-input restrictions. All scalar
metadata integers have at most 256 magnitude bits; the declared error constant
has at most 16384. Signed absolute exponents remain symbolic, including values
of magnitude 2^200. Thus this wrapper does not cover a full theorem-scale sparse
parameter instance. The accepted mathematical bridge remains more general.

The numerical guarantee is conditional on a genuine upstream ALG034 producer
contract applying to this exact input, state, precision, and output. The parser
checks declared identities, exact C, the precision inequality, target/sign/order
labels and the output digest. It cannot verify the missing ALG034 executable,
original input, phase table, rounding trace or producer authenticity. A matching
digest is a consistency check, not a proof or cryptographic authentication of
these assertions. Every returned result labels this condition explicitly.

Results from fresh controls

PASS: 338180 assertions in 169 categories, 65 malformed public calls, one full
219-operation arithmetic-ledger reconstruction and eight detected scientific
or accounting mutations. The main census includes all 6561 four-coordinate
complex vectors with Cartesian values in {-1,0,1}; signed nearest-even ties;
80 strict norm-half boundary cases; exact allowance equality and failure;
zero approximation versus an asserted exact-zero input; power-of-two signal
rescaling; final source isolation from later mutable-input changes; symbolic
exponents of both signs; and maximum permitted length and numerator width.

Both new test programs import the new wrapper. The wrapper imports unchanged,
pinned current Q16 modules to construct their exact DyadicSource class. Module
class/function declarations and that record's constructor execute; no existing
ALG034 scientific program, historical runner, Q16 window preparation, BUCKETS
call or deterministic pipeline execution runs. All scientific arithmetic in
these tests belongs to the new adapter or freshly authored rational controls.
The synthetic certificate fixtures test the conditional interface; they are not
evidence that an ALG034 producer actually emitted the supplied rows.

Boundary to Q16

On VALID_SOURCE, the returned source is the accepted exact DyadicSource class.
Its values field is an M-tuple of ((real_numerator,F),(imag_numerator,F)), every
container is an exact immutable tuple, every field an exact integer, each
Cartesian magnitude is at most one, and its Euclidean norm is strictly greater
than one half. F=16m+17, so source numerator width is at most F+1 magnitude bits.
The dense construction is new charged work and storage, not free input.

The wrapper does not accept a WindowSpec or schedules. Window compactness,
BUCKETS length/divisibility constraints, affine states, fair independent
schedules and every downstream call remain separate obligations. In particular,
M=4 or M=8 can satisfy this source boundary without authorizing BUCKETS. The
accepted deterministic pipeline supplies execution provenance once actually
called with a valid spec and schedules, but no such call occurs in this packet.

The sufficient post-production check is exact: Delta/alpha <= rho. Failure
means the sufficient published allowance is not established, not that actual
output error is known to be excessive. A failure still returns a valid source.
Zero approximation returns no normalized source and makes no claim that the
ideal target vanishes. Only the separately asserted exact-zero-input contract
has an exact-zero target, conditional on that assertion being truthful.

The second unitary negative-sign Fourier stage targets R P_(a,beta_A)x/alpha,
where R reflects indices. It does not become a full DFT of the original input.
This wrapper adds no retries, randomized recovery, arbitrary source callbacks,
external preparation receipts, dense recovery fallback or speed claim. No
Sheet, GitHub, publication, sharing-permission or parent-score edits were made.
